claims.text: Recursive prompting of ChatGPT 3.5 yields stable Large Language Model Quotient (LLMq) values beyond 40 iterations.
Qualitative coding generated by recursive LLM prompting produces results consistent with traditional coding by human evaluators.
For Text 2, LLMq values for Perception of Own Identity or Self, Novelty, and STEM Interests reached 0.900 or greater across nearly all iteration sets.
For Text 3, the code STEM Interest was identified by the LLM in 32.7% of cases after 160 iterations.

evidence.description: LLMq values calculated for each of the three texts indicate stability beyond 40 iterations for each of five codes, with trajectories flattening out.
Comparison between iteration analysis results and traditional human coding showed consistent outcomes across interview excerpts.
In Text 2 analysis, LLMq values for Perception of Own Identity or Self, Novelty, and STEM Interests were 0.900 or greater across nearly all sets of iterations.
In Text 3 analysis, the LLM reported the code STEM Interest was present in only 32.7% of cases after 160 iterations.

methodologies.name: Recursive LLM Deductive Qualitative Coding
methodologies.description: A qualitative coding framework where text excerpts and a predefined codebook are recursively submitted to an LLM across 160 iterations (logging out/in each time) to calculate a Large Language Model Quotient (LLMq) measuring code presence consensus.

limitations.text: The length of the input data is limited by the LLM's context window (e.g. ChatGPT 3.5 default limit of 2048 characters).
LLMs may struggle to accurately interpret and assign codes to noisy, unstructured, or error-containing data such as transcription errors.
Cohen's kappa allows marginal distributions to differ, measuring association rather than true agreement between raters.

future_work.text: Applying LLMs in an inductive qualitative coding process to search for emerging themes and codes within textual data.
Training LLMs on domain-specific and refined data to better reflect linguistic nuances and reduce the number of iterations required.
